identity.name: Front for the Restoration of Unity and Democracy

identity.wikipedia: Front for the Restoration of Unity and Democracy

land.text: the north of the country, where the rebels seized the military posts
the north, where the government's counter-offensive of July 1993 drove the rebels back

successors.note: Ahmed Dini's radical faction kept fighting until a final agreement in 2001; the moderate wing, led by Ali Mohamed Daoud, was given two ministries on 8 June 1995 (FRUD page).

correction.text: 'The FRUD seized all military posts in the north of the country and laid siege to the city of Tadjoura and Obock'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). The page gives no boundary and no date for the seizure; the government counter-offensive of 5 July 1993 ended it. Draw as a contest zone, not solid rebel land.

region.text: the town of Obock, assaulted on 21 November 1991

ledger.note: 1991: FRUD takes up arms in the north. 'At the beginning of October 1991, the rebel organisation Front for the Restoration of Unity and Democracy (FRUD)' began the rebellion; it 'launched, on the 21 November 1991, an assault of the town of Obock'. The FRUD page says only that groups 'merged in 1991 to form FRUD'.
1991: the northern front opens. FRUD assaulted Obock on 21 November 1991; the page names the towns, not the districts.

region.text: the north: the military posts and the sieges of Tadjoura and Obock

ledger.note: 1992: FRUD holds the north. 'The FRUD seized all military posts in the north of the country and laid siege to the city of Tadjoura and Obock' (no exact date).

region.text: the rebel-held areas of the north

ledger.note: 1993: the army drives FRUD back. 'On the 5 July 1993, the government launched a massive counter-offensive in the areas controlled by the rebels'; the FRUD base at Assa-Gueyla fell and the rebels took refuge in the mountains on the Eritrean border.
1994: FRUD signs the Abb'a agreement. 'an initial Abb'a peace agreement was signed on December 26, 1994'; the FRUD page confirms a peace agreement with the government 'on 26 December 1994 in Aba'a'.

1994: the rebel front ends as a force in the field. The movement split in 1994; the moderate wing made peace on 26 December 1994 and the radical wing under Dini 'eventually signed its own peace agreement with the government in 2001'.

wars.name: Djiboutian Civil War
wars.outcome: The government's counter-offensive of July 1993 drove FRUD back into the mountains on the Eritrean border; Abb'a agreement 26 December 1994; final agreement 12 May 2001.

certainty.note: No page opened draws FRUD's line of control; Obock and Tadjourah are the researcher's reading of 'the north'.

sources.title: Djiboutian Civil War
sources.note: FRUD's campaign: Obock 21 November 1991, the seized posts in the north, the 5 July 1993 counter-offensive, the 1994 Abb'a agreement.

sources.title: Front for the Restoration of Unity and Democracy
sources.note: Founding year (1991), leaders, the 26 December 1994 agreement, the 1994 split, entry into government (8 June 1995); gives no territory.

notes: Rebel dossier added by af-08-m because FRUD held ground in the north for about a year and a half and Cliopatria has no row. The FRUD page gives no territory and no founding month; the Civil War page names only Obock, Tadjoura, Dikhil (repelled), Assa-Gueyla (the base, no location on the page) and the Mount Mabla region (an offensive failed 3-10 March 1994). Obock and Tadjourah are the Natural Earth districts named after the towns: a wide reading. No capital is recorded: the base at Assa-Gueyla has no coordinates on the pages or in the gazetteer (listed for the gazetteer agent). The end is the 1994 agreement of the main wing; the radical wing fought until 2001.
